column1: # Style dispositions for the fifty-nine-file docs/ edit set 3a5c74b6^..937d0a1f
# sibling table (D-59). Columns, tab-separated, in this order:
#   file  ord  line  rule  token  verdict  ground  fix_sha  post_line
# `line` is relative to the named pre-edit revision 937d0a1f (Phase 157's last
# docs/ commit, before this phase's hand remediation and mechanical sweep).
# No anchor column: an anchor would be a frozen copy of a live line with no
# staleness gate, and twenty of the flagged occurrences sit on lines this
# phase itself rewrote -- the occurrence ordinal plus the revision-qualified
# line number is the key instead (D-59).
# Verdict vocabulary, exactly these seven values: EDIT | KEEP-PROTECTED |
#   EDIT           -- one of this phase's five named style edits (D-61);
#                     fix_sha and post_line name the real landed commit.
#   SWEPT          -- tightened by the mechanical em-dash sweep (44ab8c21).
#   KEEP-PROTECTED -- sits in a structural class sweep3.py already protects
#                     (here: every occurrence is a table row -- sweep3.py
#                     skips any line starting with "|" outright).
#   MASK-ARTIFACT  -- check.py's own mask_code() manufactured the match: it
#                     blanks a markdown link target to spaces of equal
#                     length, and the em-dash-spaced rule then fires on that
#                     manufactured whitespace rather than real prose.
#   KEEP-BY-RULE   -- the word-list or voice entry's own scope, sense, or
#                     named exemption does not actually cover this occurrence
#                     (a parser artifact, a proper noun, a different sense of
#                     the word, or a self-contradictory scoped entry); ground
#                     names the specific mismatch, never the phrase "product
#   KEEP-FLAGGED   -- a genuine candidate under the rule's own definition,
#                     left un-rewritten this phase; every passive occurrence
#                     is KEEP-FLAGGED without exception (D-39/D-61: no actor
#                     is invented for a sentence that withheld one).
#   NO-CANDIDATES  -- one of the twenty-seven edited files in this range that
#                     carries neither a candidate nor a sweep edit on any
# _load_module() helper imports check.py's RULES/mask_code and sweep3.py's
# structural classifiers by file location, in process -- no enumeration
# script, no per-file-fragment method. Whole-file structural-rule and
# word-list hits are computed once per file, then intersected with that
# file's added-line numbers from the range diff (both cited derivations of
# Measured, not copied: 184 added lines (27 blank, 24 mask-blanked template
# 158-CONTEXT.md D-11 exactly. 94 raw occurrences (47 word-list / 25 passive /
# 19 em-dash-spaced / 3 directional) across 53 lines in 32 files -- matches
# D-59/D-60 exactly. Two divergences from the written record, both recorded
# rather than forced to match: (1) check.py's own RULES independently fire
# BOTH the "directional" structural rule and a separate word-list "above"
# entry on the identical token at docs/_standards/EEE-SOP-standard.md:658;
# both are resolved by the single fix_sha 3c53f72a edit, so the duplicate
# word-list finding is folded into that one EDIT row (keyed under
# "directional") rather than given a second row -- any other verdict on that
# second row would fail the post-edit byte-identity re-proof, since the line
# genuinely changed. This drops the table to 93 occurrence rows, not 94.
# (2) Twenty-seven of the fifty-nine files carry neither a candidate nor a
# sweep edit, not the twenty-six D-59 recorded -- one additional _templates/
# file's added lines are entirely mask-blanked (docs/_glossary-macos.md and
# eight docs/_templates/*.md files all resolve to zero scannable candidates).
